discovery: Event-horizon-scale imaging of supermassive black holes (M87* and Sgr A*) with the Event Horizon Telescope

nominees.name: Sheperd S. Doeleman
nominees.affiliation: Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

subfield: Astrophysics / black hole physics / very-long-baseline interferometry
motivation: For decades, stellar orbits established that a compact object of four million solar masses sits at the centre of our Galaxy, but they could not resolve the event horizon itself. Heino Falcke predicted (2000) that the black hole 'shadow' of Sgr A* would be observable with millimetre VLBI; Sheperd Doeleman led the technical campaign—wideband recording, new stations, phased ALMA—that first detected horizon-scale structure (2008) and built the Event Horizon Telescope into an Earth-sized instrument. The resulting images of M87* (2019) and Sgr A* (2022), confirmed by repeated independent imaging pipelines and multi-year observations showing a persistent ring, turned black hole horizons from a theoretical construct into directly imaged objects consistent with general relativity. This is a triumph of technology opening a new window, and it launched precision tests of gravity in the strong-field regime.
